voice: Fluent, intelligent, sensual, and strategic, with genuine grief for Ernie and no phonetic French caricature; adjacent speakers retain their established voices.

entries.text: Steve! Something terrible has happened. Ernie is dead!
Ernie?
Yes, my Ernie. What am I going to do? Please, I need someone with me. Come into my office.
Sorry, Miss Bow. The poor woman seems very upset. Maybe there's something I can do for her.
I can imagine.
We can talk more later, okay?
We'll see about that.
Hmm...
Thank you for coming, Olympia. It was kind of you.
You're very welcome, dear girl. What can I do for you?
I found this strange bone, and I thought, if anyone could identify it, Olympia could.
A bone, you say? How fascinating. Where did you find it?
I found it here in the museum. Here it is.
Now, let me see...
Ha! Yvette, you tease. This is a chicken bone!
It is?
Of course. Why, it is still greasy. You took this from dinner, didn't you?
*giggle* You caught me. It was a little joke.
You are incorrigible, Yvette, but I am quite fond of you.
Olympia, we are good friends, aren't we? There is something I need to discuss with you.
Oh? Certainly. What is it?
Come closer. It is very personal, and I do not want anyone to overhear.
Oh, my. Oh, my... Oh, MY!
Oh, my.
How does that feel?
Magnificent. Mmm.
I'm not rubbing too hard, am I?
The harder, the better, mon ami.
Well, we all get a little stiff now and then.
You are very good at finding the knots. Mmm.
Would you mind not moaning so loudly? You might draw attention.
I cannot help it. You are so big and strong.
Oh, my...
Well, Yvette, we've known each other a long time. I'm not ready for marriage, but I know one thing: I love you.
My great detective... I feel the same.
Keep in mind that if I ever catch you with another man, I'll kill you.
What? Oh, that is one of your jokes, yes? Such a fine sense of humor.
I've already had one bad marriage, and it won't happen again. It's been a long time since I've trusted anyone as much as I trust you.
That is very flattering, my love. I have never known anyone like you, either. You are so good and kind.
I try. It isn't easy being a cop in this town. The place is lousy with criminals, even on the police force.
Oh, no. How terrible!

It's a hard thing when a cop goes bad. I've seen it happen. A man spends years fighting crime, watching crooks grow rich while he risks his neck for a few dollars. The first bribe troubles him. The next one comes easier.
You are such a strong man, Ryan. You would never accept a payoff, would you?
I'm shocked you'd even ask such a thing, Yvette!
I'm sorry, my love. I should have known better.
You'll have to show me how sorry you are. Kiss me.
Gladly, my love. How can I resist?
You lied to me!
Then that makes us even. You lied to me.
You had something to do with the Dagger burglary!
You've been sleeping with someone else! I saw you leave with that dockworker.
I have never slept with Steve! And Ziggy told me about you and the Dagger.
And you believed that little weasel? I've arrested him more times than I can count!
I have known Ziggy for a long time. He would not lie to me.
That man would lie to his own mother if someone paid him for it!
Ziggy said you were working with Carrington to steal the Dagger!
Lies! You cannot trust him. If he were not already dead, I'd beat the truth out of him!
Maybe you already did.
Were you sleeping with that little rat, then?
Of course not!
You surprise me, Yvette. Accusing me of burglary--anyone would think you were raised in the streets.
Where I grew up does not matter. What matters is--wait. Did you hear something at the door?
Yes. I heard it too. Keep your voice down.
